original.target_description: Independent-samples comparison of unattended-channel ERP mean amplitudes (100–200 ms, collapsed across linguistic/nonlinguistic probes) between higher and lower maternal education groups; 32 children aged 3–8 years, 16 per group.

n.sample_role: Children contributing to the independent-samples unattended-channel ERP comparison; 16 per maternal education group.
n.exclusions: Selected subset of 53 previously studied typically developing children, chosen to maximize SES differences while balancing experimental conditions. Monolingual English, no neurological/language disorder, normal screening, receptive language above 25th percentile. All children had at least 78 usable trials per bin.
n.location: Method, Participants; Table 1, N row, both maternal education columns; Results, ERP Results (test df=30).
n.quote: Higher Maternal Education Lower Maternal Education N 16 16

es.location: p. 640 (input locator); Results, ERP Results, supplemental comparison of unattended-channel responses, paragraph beginning “Attentional modulation involves two processes”. HTML pagination not independently verified.
es.quote: the groups did differ in response to probe stimuli in the unattended channel, independent samples t (30) = −2.87, P < .01

p.location: p. 640 (input locator); Results, ERP Results, supplemental comparison of unattended-channel responses. HTML pagination not independently verified.

replication.target_description: Located the cited paper’s Hypothesis 1 correlation of cumulative SES risk (income, maternal education, marital status) with unattended ERP amplitudes, in 100 Head Start children aged 3–5. This is not a maternal-education-only test; retained as the authors’ identified conceptual replication with that mismatch explicit.

n.sample_role: Children included in final analyses of cumulative SES risk and unattended ERP amplitudes.
n.exclusions: EEG obtained from 123 children; excluded eight tested in Spanish, 13 declining ECG electrodes, one with unusable impedance cardiogram, and one with missing socioeconomic information. Task inclusion required at least seven of 12 comprehension questions correct.
n.location: Method, Participants, final sentence; Table 1 describes this final sample.
n.quote: Therefore, final analyses included 100 children (50 females) ranging in age from 3–5 years old

es.location: Table 2, row 4 “Unattended ERP amplitudes”, column 2 “SES risks”; Results, Hypothesis 1, first sentence (input locator p. 1679; HTML pagination not independently verified).
es.quote: SES risk was positively associated with mean amplitude of ERPs elicited by unattended probes during the dichotic listening task [ r (98) = .21, p = .037]

p.location: Results, “Hypothesis 1: Early adversity impacts selective attention”, first sentence (input locator p. 1679; HTML pagination not independently verified). Table 2 row 4/column 2 marks the same correlation with one star, p < .05.

reported_success.location: Discussion, paragraph beginning “As noted, this study builds on a small body of research”.
reported_success.quote: Here, we replicate this finding in a larger sample of one-hundred 3–5 year old children enrolled in Head Start using a cumulative risk framework to characterize SES.

notes: Both titles and DOIs verified in full-text PMC author manuscripts. Extracted printed values without conversion. Replication uses a cumulative SES index, not maternal education alone, so target_match is false despite the authors’ successful-replication narrative. PMC replication manuscript explicitly reports final n=100; do not mix it with other versions or generic abstract totals. HTML has no independently verified print-page mapping; section/table locators supplied for reproducibility. Original requested test statistic is retained as t rather than converted effect size.
